problem_type: natural-language director plans lose entity and camera-motion intent
symptom: S1 plans frequently return generic or missing actors and shot subjects, producing low correspondence and motion/blocking scores; vehicle chase plans may not yield a measurable follow camera.
direct_cause: Planner examples contain benchmark-like courtyard and perfume scenes, while the prompt does not make user noun preservation, exact kind/template selection, shot subject coverage, or movement semantics a hard contract; the compiler also uses a generic fallback trajectory when a follow shot has no materialized motion.
class_root: Every natural-language entity and requested shot must converge through one shared plan contract: user nouns are retained in actor/scene names and refs, kinds/templates/moves use legal enums, every shot names an existing subject, and moving subjects provide a camera co-motion trajectory.
internal_only_reason: The invariant is an internal Director Plan v2 contract and deterministic compiler boundary; no external service decides entity naming or camera trajectory semantics.
invariants: Planner examples are outside the evaluation card scenes and preserve no benchmark answer.
Actor descriptions and set-piece kinds retain user nouns, each shot.subject resolves to an actor or actor anchor, and legal kind/template/move enums are used.
A follow shot over a moving actor has camera and subject co-motion with stable framing rather than a stationary or fabricated actor path.

Compiler entity ids are derived only from plan names: actor:<id>, shot:<id>/camera, setPiece:<id>; repeated compilation is byte-for-byte deterministic and a local plan rename changes only its entity id.
Every person has a valid action clip covering t=0; stacked on-relations preserve vertical separation and product_stage always materializes s1-product-ground.

door_reduction.why_not: Compiler type boundaries and the model-facing schema are separate public contracts consumed by different gates and callers; keeping all three makes each changed boundary auditable.

generality_proof: All S1 requests enter through planDirector and then compileDirectorPlan; the schema and compiler are shared by every card and by hand-authored oracle plans. Enforcing the invariant in the prompt/schema-facing planner and the follow trajectory solver covers different scenes, actor kinds, and retries without card IDs or aliases.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Constrain every model response to preserve user nouns, choose legal enums, and provide complete shot coverage.
Compile moving-subject follow shots with camera co-motion and stable aim.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: All live S1 planner requests call planDirector and then compileDirectorPlan.
Hand-authored and retry-normalized plans share compileDirectorPlan, including follow motion.

recurrence.reason: Any new brief can use different nouns, actor kinds, scene templates, or moving vehicles and reproduce the same generic binding or unmeasurable follow motion.

prevention.invariant: Each response must use original user nouns for entity descriptions/refs, legal enum values, and existing subjects for every shot; compiler follow motion must co-move with an actor trajectory, stable entity ids must not include a plan hash, every person must have action evidence from t=0, and stacked product props must remain separated.
prevention.failure_mode: Schema errors are returned with exact paths and retried once; unresolved plans become adapter_error, while compiler issues remain explicit and no half-built project is returned.
prevention.strategy: Make the rule explicit at the only model boundary and keep deterministic motion handling at the only compiler boundary used by both live and oracle plans.

legacy_paths.rationale: No persisted legacy plan format or fallback compiler is removed; this repair strengthens the existing v2 boundary.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: The failure is in our prompt and compiler invariants; the existing fetch client and action library do not own entity binding or camera co-motion.

migration: No migration is needed because plans are transient eval inputs and schema v2 remains unchanged.
residual_risks: L5 visual quality and Windows packaged runtime remain unverified.
The external scorer and card binding are intentionally out of scope and may expose additional ruler issues.

invariant_owner_layer.why: The planner is the only shared natural-language boundary; compiler tests cover the downstream trajectory invariant.
